title: Flavoring in Flutter
abstract: Flutter flavors allow developers to create multiple versions of an app from a single codebase, each with its own configurations, assets, and settings. This is particularly useful for managing different environments (development, staging, production) or branding variations (free vs. paid versions). By defining flavors in the build configuration files and using conditional imports, developers can easily switch between different app versions during development and deployment. This approach enhances code maintainability and streamlines the release process.

title: From Code to the Web
abstract: This section provides a detailed guide on deploying a Flutter web application. It explains how to create a Flutter web project, test it locally, build it for production using WebAssembly (Wasm), and deploy it on GitHub Pages. The guide includes commands for enabling web support, running the app locally, building the app with the --wasm flag for optimized performance, and deploying it manually or via GitHub Actions. It also covers setting up a custom domain for GitHub Pages.

title: One Codebase to Rule Them All
abstract: Flutter is a versatile framework that enables developers to create high-performance, multi-platform applications using a single Dart codebase. By leveraging its custom rendering engine, Skia, Flutter ensures consistent UI and predictable performance across platforms like Android, iOS, Web, Windows, macOS, and Linux. Its widget-based architecture promotes code reusability, while tools like Hot Reload enhance productivity. With centralized build commands and support for platform-specific adaptations, Flutter redefines cross-platform development, offering a seamless balance between efficiency and performance.
